Question 1
?

Calculate f′(x) for f(x)=arctan⁡(arcsec(x2)).

a
2xx4−1(1+arcsec2(x2))
b
2xx2+1(1−arcsec(x2))
c
1xx2−1(1+arcsec2(x2))
d
1x4−1(1+arcsec2(x2))
e
2x4−1(1+arcsec(x2))
Submit

decision.explanation: By the chain rule, f'(x) = (1/(1+arcsec²(x²)))·(2x/(|x²|√(x⁴−1))). Since |x²|=x², this simplifies to 2/[x√(x⁴−1)(1+arcsec²(x²))], for |x|>1.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
The formulae for the derivatives of $arctan$ and $arcsec$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arctanx) & =\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsecx) & =\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the chain rule and the formulae above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(arcsec({x}^{2}))) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(arcsec({x}^{2}))^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsec({x}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(arcsec({x}^{2}))^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}|\sqrt{({x}^{2})^{2}-1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(arcsec({x}^{2}))^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}|\sqrt{({x}^{2})^{2}-1}}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{2}{x\sqrt{{x}^{4}-1}(1+{arcsec}^{2}({x}^{2}))}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
The formulae for the derivatives of $arctan$ and $arcsec$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arctanx) & =\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsecx) & =\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the chain rule and the formulae above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(arcsec({x}^{2}))) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(arcsec({x}^{2}))^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsec({x}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(arcsec({x}^{2}))^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}|\sqrt{({x}^{2})^{2}-1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(arcsec({x}^{2}))^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}|\sqrt{({x}^{2})^{2}-1}}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{2}{x\sqrt{{x}^{4}-1}(1+{arcsec}^{2}({x}^{2}))}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find f′(x) if f(x)=2arcsec(6x−1).

a
−6|6x−1|9x2−3x
b

decision.explanation: Using the chain rule, f'(x)=12/(|6x-1|√((6x-1)²-1)). Since (6x-1)²-1=4(9x²-3x), the square root contributes a factor of 2, giving 6/(|6x-1|√(9x²-3x)).

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of $arcsec$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsecx)=\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2arcsec(6x-1)) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsec(6x-1)) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{|6x-1|\sqrt{(6x-1)^{2}-1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6x-1) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{|6x-1|\sqrt{{(6x-1)}^{2}-1}}\cdot 6 \\  & =\frac{12}{|6x-1|\sqrt{36{x}^{2}-12x}} \\  & =\frac{12}{|6x-1|\sqrt{4(9{x}^{2}-3x)}} \\  & =\frac{6}{|6x-1|\sqrt{9{x}^{2}-3x}}.\end{aligned}
$$
